settings.summary: How sharp floors and walls stay when you look along them.
settings.details: The number is the filtering level, 2× up to 16×. Higher levels keep textures seen at a shallow angle sharper and can cost performance on some systems. Your graphics hardware caps the level the game can actually use.

settings.name: r_aspectRatio
settings.title: Picture proportions
settings.summary: Chooses whether the picture is drawn for a 4:3, 16:10 or 16:9 screen, or follows your display.
settings.details: Auto follows your display. The game scales your mouse turn with the picture's width, so the same Mouse speed turns about 13% farther at 16:10 and about 21% farther at 16:9 than at 4:3. It is a latched setting and applies after the renderer restarts.

settings.name: r_blur
settings.title: Screen blur
settings.summary: How much the whole picture is blurred.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_borderless
settings.title: Borderless full screen
settings.summary: Fills the screen with a borderless window instead of changing the display mode.
settings.details: This setting comes from the macOS version of the game. The launcher's display settings cover it for most players.

settings.name: r_clearColor
settings.title: Screen clear colour
settings.summary: A colour the renderer clears the screen to before drawing.
settings.details: Its exact use is not documented. The default is black.

settings.name: r_clearColor2
settings.title: Second clear colour
settings.summary: A second colour the renderer clears the screen to.
settings.details: Its exact use is not documented. The default is black.

settings.name: r_colorMap
settings.title: Colour map override
settings.summary: A developer switch that replaces colour maps with white or black.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_cosinePowerMapShift
settings.title: Specular power shift
settings.summary: A developer value that shifts the specular power map.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_debugEntCounts
settings.title: Entity count debug
settings.summary: A renderer developer aid.
settings.details: A developer aid; its effect is not documented here.

settings.name: r_debugShader
settings.title: Shader debug view
settings.summary: A developer switch for viewing shader debug information.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_depthPrepassModels
settings.title: Model depth pre-pass
settings.summary: Draws model depth in a first pass before the models themselves.
settings.details: Off by default, and the game's safe mode sets it to off. Its effect is inferred from the name.

settings.name: r_displayRefresh
settings.title: Screen refresh rate
settings.summary: Which refresh rate the game asks your display for.
settings.details: The game builds this list from your display at start-up, so the catalog cannot list the rates. It is a latched setting, and the rate you get depends on your display.

settings.name: r_distortion
settings.title: Heat haze
settings.summary: Bends the picture around heat sources such as flames and explosions.
settings.details: Heat haze is one of the DirectX 9 effects, and competitive configs in the research often turn it off. Nothing in the research measures its cost.

settings.name: r_dlightLimit
settings.title: Dynamic lights
settings.summary: How many moving lights, such as muzzle flashes and explosions, the game draws at once.
settings.details: The game's menu offers Off (0), Low (2), Normal (4) and High (8); the setting accepts 0 to 32. More lights cost frame rate in firefights.

settings.name: r_drawBModels
settings.title: Draw brush models
settings.summary: A developer switch for drawing brush models.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_drawDecals
settings.title: Draw wall marks
settings.summary: Whether wall marks are drawn.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. Turn Bullet marks off to remove marks instead. ESL's old PunkBuster list required it on.

settings.name: r_drawEntities
settings.title: Draw entities
settings.summary: A developer switch for drawing entities.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. ESL's old PunkBuster list required it on.

settings.name: r_drawPrimCap
settings.title: Draw primitive cap
settings.summary: A developer value that limits how many primitives are drawn.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. ESL's old PunkBuster list required 0.

settings.name: r_drawPrimFloor
settings.title: Draw primitive floor
settings.summary: A developer value that sets a minimum for primitives drawn.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. ESL's old PunkBuster list required 0.

settings.name: r_drawSModels
settings.title: Draw static models
settings.summary: A developer switch for drawing static models.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. ESL's old PunkBuster list required it on.

settings.name: r_drawSun
settings.title: Draw the sun
settings.summary: Shows or hides the sun and the glare it causes.
settings.details: Turning it off removes the sun and the sun-blind darkening, and can help performance slightly, according to TweakGuide. zPAM sets it to off for every player when they join a team.

settings.name: r_drawWater
settings.title: Draw water
settings.summary: Whether water is drawn.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. WWCL's old rules required it on.

settings.name: r_drawWorld
settings.title: Draw the world
settings.summary: A developer switch for drawing the world geometry.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_drawXModels
settings.title: Draw models
settings.summary: A developer switch for drawing models.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_fog
settings.title: Fog
settings.summary: Whether the game draws fog.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. ESL's old PunkBuster list and WWCL's old rules required fog on.

settings.name: r_forceLod
settings.title: Force model detail
settings.summary: Forces every model to one level of detail.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. WWCL's old rules required it left on none.

settings.name: r_fullbright
settings.title: Full brightness
settings.summary: Draws everything fully lit, without shading.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. It removes shadowing, so rule sets forbid it: ESL's old PunkBuster list and WWCL's old rules required it off.

settings.name: r_fullscreen
settings.title: Full-screen display
settings.summary: Chooses full screen or a window.
settings.details: CoD2x lets you change this: on is full screen and off is a window, and a window the size of your display gives borderless play. It is latched, so a change applies after the renderer restarts.

settings.name: r_gamma
settings.title: Brightness
settings.summary: How bright the picture is; 1 is normal.
settings.details: The game's own slider runs from 0.5 to 3. Higher is brighter, and 3 is very bright. The renderer applies it through the display's brightness curve, so what you see also depends on your display.

settings.name: r_glow
settings.title: Glow effects
settings.summary: Adds a soft glow around bright parts of the picture.
settings.details: Turning it off can noticeably improve performance, especially on weaker graphics cards, and some players find the glow distracting. It is a DirectX 9 effect. Published pro configs mostly turn it off.

settings.name: r_glowBloomCutoff
settings.title: Glow brightness cutoff
settings.summary: A tuning value for the glow effect.
settings.details: It likely sets the brightness above which things glow, inferred from its name.

settings.name: r_glowBloomDesaturation
settings.title: Glow colour drain
settings.summary: A tuning value for the glow effect.
settings.details: It likely sets how much colour the glow loses, inferred from its name.

settings.name: r_glowBloomIntensity0
settings.title: First glow strength
settings.summary: A tuning value for the glow effect.
settings.details: It likely sets how strong the first glow is, inferred from its name. Map scripts set this when a map loads, so a value you save may be replaced.

settings.name: r_glowBloomIntensity1
settings.title: Second glow strength
settings.summary: A tuning value for the glow effect.
settings.details: It likely sets how strong the second glow is, inferred from its name. Map scripts set this when a map loads, so a value you save may be replaced.

settings.name: r_glowRadius0
settings.title: First glow radius
settings.summary: A tuning value for the glow effect.
settings.details: It likely sets how far the first glow spreads, inferred from its name.

settings.name: r_glowRadius1
settings.title: Second glow radius
settings.summary: A tuning value for the glow effect.
settings.details: It likely sets how far the second glow spreads, inferred from its name.

settings.name: r_glowSkyBleedIntensity0
settings.title: First glow sky bleed
settings.summary: A tuning value for the glow effect.
settings.details: It likely sets how much the first glow bleeds in from the sky, inferred from its name. Map scripts set this when a map loads, so a value you save may be replaced.

settings.name: r_glowSkyBleedIntensity1
settings.title: Second glow sky bleed
settings.summary: A tuning value for the glow effect.
settings.details: It likely sets how much the second glow bleeds in from the sky, inferred from its name.

settings.name: r_gpuSync
settings.title: CPU and GPU syncing
settings.summary: How strictly the game keeps your processor and graphics card in step.
settings.details: Choices are off, beginning, before present and adaptive, and adaptive is the default. Lower settings can raise frame rate but may add mouse and keyboard lag, which is why the game's makers chose adaptive.

settings.name: r_highLodDist
settings.title: High detail distance
settings.summary: A developer value for the distance that uses high model detail.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_ignore
settings.title: Renderer ignore flags
settings.summary: A renderer developer aid.
settings.details: A developer aid; its effect is not documented here.

settings.name: r_ignorehwgamma
settings.title: Ignore display gamma
settings.summary: Tells the game not to use the display's hardware brightness curve.
settings.details: The exact effect is not documented. It is latched, so a change applies after the renderer restarts.

settings.name: r_inGameVideo
settings.title: In-game video
settings.summary: Plays video that appears on in-game screens.
settings.details: On by default.

settings.name: r_lightMap
settings.title: Lightmap override
settings.summary: A developer switch that replaces lightmaps with white or black.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. WWCL's old rules required it left on unchanged.

settings.name: r_lightTweakAmbient
settings.title: Model ambient light
settings.summary: Adds extra ambient light to models.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. ESL's old PunkBuster list allowed 0 to 0.2 and ePAM forced 0.

settings.name: r_lightTweakAmbientColor
settings.title: Ambient light colour
settings.summary: A developer colour for the extra ambient light.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_lightTweakDiffuseFraction
settings.title: Diffuse light share
settings.summary: A developer value for how much of the tweaked light is diffuse.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_lightTweakSunColor
settings.title: Sun light colour
settings.summary: A developer colour for the tweaked sun light.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_lightTweakSunDiffuseColor
settings.title: Sun diffuse colour
settings.summary: A developer colour for the tweaked diffuse sun light.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_lightTweakSunDirection
settings.title: Sun light direction
settings.summary: A developer direction for the tweaked sun light.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_lightTweakSunLight
settings.title: Sun light strength
settings.summary: A developer value for the tweaked sun light.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_lockPvs
settings.title: Lock visibility
settings.summary: A developer switch that freezes what the game considers visible.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_lodBias
settings.title: Model detail bias
settings.summary: Pushes distant models toward more detail.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. Its range is -1000 to 0, and ESL's old PunkBuster list allowed -200 to 0.

settings.name: r_lodScale
settings.title: Distant model detail
settings.summary: How soon models in the distance switch to simpler versions.
settings.details: Stock CoD2 protects this setting and allows 1 to 4. CoD2x unlocks it and allows 0 to 1, saved with your config, and 1 is the default. ESL's old PunkBuster list and ePAM both required 1, and ClanBase's old enforcer blocked changing it.

settings.name: r_logFile
settings.title: Renderer log file
settings.summary: A renderer developer aid.
settings.details: A developer aid; its effect is not documented here.

settings.name: r_lowestLodDist
settings.title: Lowest detail distance
settings.summary: A developer value for the distance that uses the lowest model detail.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_lowLodDist
settings.title: Low detail distance
settings.summary: A developer value for the distance that uses low model detail.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_mediumLodDist
settings.title: Medium detail distance
settings.summary: A developer value for the distance that uses medium model detail.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_mode
settings.title: Display resolution
settings.summary: The size of the picture the game draws.
settings.details: The game's menu calls this Video Mode. On macOS the list is built from your display's available modes when the game starts, so the catalog cannot list the sizes. It is latched and applies after the renderer restarts.

settings.name: r_monitor
settings.title: Monitor number
settings.summary: Which monitor the game uses in full screen.
settings.details: From 0 to 8, and the name suggests the monitor's position in the list. It is latched, so a change applies after the renderer restarts.

settings.name: r_multiGpu
settings.title: Multi-GPU tuning
settings.summary: Tunes the game for computers with more than one graphics card.
settings.details: The game's menu calls this Optimize for SLI. Guides warn it can add mouse and keyboard lag, and the game leaves it off by default.

settings.name: r_norefresh
settings.title: Skip screen refresh
settings.summary: A developer switch that stops the screen being refreshed.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_normalMap
settings.title: Normal map override
settings.summary: A developer switch that replaces normal maps with flat ones.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_objectiveColorDx7Max
settings.title: Objective colour, high
settings.summary: The brighter colour used for objectives in the DirectX 7 renderer.
settings.details: Its role is inferred from its name.

settings.name: r_objectiveColorDx7Min
settings.title: Objective colour, low
settings.summary: The darker colour used for objectives in the DirectX 7 renderer.
settings.details: Its role is inferred from its name.

settings.name: r_optimize
settings.title: Optimise geometry on load
settings.summary: Tidies map geometry when a map loads.
settings.details: On by default. It is latched, so a change applies after the renderer restarts.

settings.name: r_optimizeLightmaps
settings.title: Optimise lightmaps on load
settings.summary: Tidies a map's baked lighting when it loads.
settings.details: On by default. It is latched, so a change applies after the renderer restarts.

settings.name: r_optimizeXModels
settings.title: Optimise models on load
settings.summary: How hard the game tidies model data when a map loads.
settings.details: From 0 to 1,000, and 100 by default. It is latched, so a change applies after the renderer restarts.

settings.name: r_outdoorAwayBias
settings.title: Outdoor away bias
settings.summary: A renderer tuning value for outdoor scenes.
settings.details: Its exact effect is not documented.

settings.name: r_outdoorDownBias
settings.title: Outdoor down bias
settings.summary: A renderer tuning value for outdoor scenes.
settings.details: Its exact effect is not documented.

settings.name: r_outdoorFeather
settings.title: Outdoor feather
settings.summary: A renderer tuning value for outdoor scenes.
settings.details: Its exact effect is not documented.

settings.name: r_overbrightBits
settings.title: Light intensity scaling
settings.summary: Scales how bright map lighting is drawn.
settings.details: Believed to scale baked lighting intensity, from its Quake heritage. The setting accepts 0 or 1 and is latched. ESL's old PunkBuster list allowed 0 to 2.

settings.name: r_picmip
settings.title: Texture detail
settings.summary: How sharp surface textures look, from Extra (sharpest) down to Low.
settings.details: 0 is Extra, 1 is High, 2 is Normal and 3 is Low, the same order as the game's own Texture Resolution menu. Sharper textures use more memory. Automatic texture settings can override this unless Choose texture detail yourself is on. Rule sets disagree about level 3, so 0 to 2 is the conservative range.

settings.name: r_picmip_bump
settings.title: Surface relief detail
settings.summary: How sharp the textures that give surfaces their small bumps look, on the same Extra to Low scale.
settings.details: 0 is Extra, 1 is High, 2 is Normal and 3 is Low, matching the game's Normal Map Resolution menu. It is only used when Choose texture detail yourself is on.

settings.name: r_picmip_manual
settings.title: Choose texture detail yourself
settings.summary: Uses the texture detail levels you pick instead of letting the game choose.
settings.details: The game's menu calls this Texture Quality, with Automatic and Manual. With it off, the game's automatic settings pick the detail, and the three texture detail settings are not used.

settings.name: r_picmip_spec
settings.title: Shine texture detail
settings.summary: How sharp the textures that make surfaces shine look, on the same Extra to Low scale.
settings.details: 0 is Extra, 1 is High, 2 is Normal and 3 is Low, matching the game's Specular Map Resolution menu. It is only used when Choose texture detail yourself is on.

settings.name: r_polygonOffsetBias
settings.title: Mark depth offset
settings.summary: Pushes wall marks and overlays toward or away from the surface they sit on.
settings.details: From -16 to 16, and -1 by default. Large values make bullet marks and overlay textures disappear, which some players use to spot enemies more easily. Rule sets treat unusual values as suspect: ESL's old PunkBuster list allowed -1 to 16 and a later PunkBuster template required exactly -1.

settings.name: r_polygonOffsetScale
settings.title: Mark depth slope
settings.summary: Adjusts the same wall-mark depth offset on sloped surfaces.
settings.details: From -4 to 4, and -1 by default. Unusual values are treated as suspect: ESL's old PunkBuster list allowed -1 to 4.

settings.name: r_portalBevels
settings.title: Portal bevel amount
settings.summary: A renderer tuning value for portal visibility.
settings.details: From 0 to 1, and 0.7 by default. It is saved with your config. Its exact effect is not documented.

settings.name: r_portalBevelsOnly
settings.title: Portal bevels only
settings.summary: A renderer tuning switch for portal visibility.
settings.details: A developer aid; its effect is not documented here.

settings.name: r_portalFineCull
settings.title: Fine portal culling
settings.summary: A developer switch for portal visibility culling.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_portalMinClipArea
settings.title: Portal minimum area
settings.summary: A renderer tuning value for portal visibility.
settings.details: From 0 to 1, and 0.02 by default. Its exact effect is not documented.

settings.name: r_portalWalkLimit
settings.title: Portal walk limit
settings.summary: A developer value that limits portal visibility walking.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_presentMode
settings.title: Frame presenting mode
settings.summary: Chooses whether the game skips showing a frame while the last one is still being drawn.
settings.details: 0 shows every frame. 1 waits for the graphics card to finish the previous frame and, if it has not, skips showing this one so the screen never shows an older picture. It comes from the macOS version of the game and is saved with your config.

settings.name: r_pvsStats
settings.title: Visibility statistics
settings.summary: A renderer developer aid.
settings.details: A developer aid; its effect is not documented here.

settings.name: r_railCoreWidth
settings.title: Rail beam width
settings.summary: A leftover Quake 3 setting for the width of a rail beam.
settings.details: No effect is known in CoD2.

settings.name: r_rendererInUse
settings.title: Renderer in use
settings.summary: Which drawing method the game is using right now.
settings.details: The game sets it itself and treats it as read-only. Choices are none, DirectX 9 and DirectX 7.

settings.name: r_rendererPreference
settings.title: Drawing method
settings.summary: Which of the game's original drawing methods it prefers.
settings.details: Choices are Auto, DirectX 9 and DirectX 7, and DirectX 9 is the default. It is latched and applies after the renderer restarts. The catalog neither adds a Metal renderer nor promises that any listed method is available.

settings.name: r_showFbColorDebug
settings.title: Framebuffer colour debug
settings.summary: A developer switch for showing framebuffer colours.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_showFloatZDebug
settings.title: Floating depth debug

settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_showGroundLit
settings.title: Show ground lighting

settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_showLightGrid
settings.title: Show light grid
settings.summary: A developer switch for showing the light grid.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_showMissingLightGrid
settings.title: Show missing light grid
settings.summary: A developer switch for showing where the light grid is missing.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_showPortals

settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_showSModelNames
settings.title: Show static model names

settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_showTriCounts
settings.title: Show triangle counts

settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_showTris
settings.title: Show wireframe

settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. ESL's old PunkBuster list required it off.

settings.name: r_showVertCounts
settings.title: Show vertex counts

settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_singleCell
settings.title: Single visibility cell
settings.summary: A developer switch that limits drawing to one visibility cell.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_skinCache
settings.title: Cache model skins

settings.details: On by default. TweakGuide says to turn it off only on very low memory.

settings.name: r_skipBackEnd

settings.name: r_skipPvs

settings.details: On by default.

settings.name: r_specularColorScale
settings.title: Specular colour scale

settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: r_sunblind_min_angle
settings.title: Sun-blind start angle

settings.name: r_sunflare_fadein
settings.title: Sun flare fade in
settings.summary: How many seconds the sun flare takes to appear.
settings.details: From 0 to 60 seconds, and 1 by default. Maps likely set the sun themselves.

settings.name: r_sunglare_min_angle

settings.name: r_sunsprite_size

settings.details: The game's menu calls this Sync Every Frame. With it on, frames per second cannot go above your display's refresh rate. It is a latched setting, so it applies after the renderer restarts, and what happens in the end depends on your graphics driver.

settings.name: sensitivity

settings.summary: How far your view turns when you move the mouse.
settings.details: A higher number turns farther for the same hand movement. The game's own slider runs from 1 to 30 and ESL's old PunkBuster list also stops at 30; the setting itself accepts 0.01 to 100, and values below 1 are valid. The game also scales your turn with the picture's field of view, so the same number turns a little farther in a wider window and slower while you zoom in. Your mouse's DPI is separate.

settings.details: CoD2x only. Without it, mounted guns ignore Mouse speed and turn at a fixed rate. With it, this number is used in place of Mouse speed while you man one, and Mouse acceleration still adds to it. The default is 1, and it accepts 0.01 to 100.

settings.title: Game version
settings.summary: The version number this build reports to servers.
settings.details: The game fills this in itself and treats it as read-only. The CoD2x build reports 1.4.6.8 where stock reports 1.3.

settings.name: showdrop
settings.title: Show dropped packets
settings.summary: Prints a note when a packet is dropped.
settings.details: A developer aid. It is off by default.

settings.name: showpackets
settings.title: Show every packet
settings.summary: Prints every packet sent and received.
settings.details: A developer aid. It is off by default and floods the console.

settings.name: snaps
settings.title: Updates you receive
settings.summary: How many game updates per second you ask the server to send you.
settings.details: Your request is a ceiling: the server's own update rate also limits how often you get one. Stock servers cap it at 30 and CoD2x servers at 40. Servers using CoD2x competitive rules enforce 40, and zPAM 3 servers on stock CoD2 expect 30.
runtimeNotes: CoD2x server policy can change the value, type or limits at run time; registration metadata is not a live ruleset.

settings.name: snd_bits
settings.title: Sound depth
settings.summary: How many bits of detail each sound sample uses.
settings.details: From 8 to 16 bits, and 16 by default. TweakGuide says 8 can improve performance at the cost of quality. It is latched, so a change applies after the game restarts.

settings.name: snd_enable2D
settings.title: 2D sounds
settings.summary: Whether the game plays 2D sounds such as menu clicks and music.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. Turning it off would silence 2D sounds, which TweakGuide lists as button clicks and music.

settings.name: snd_enable3D
settings.title: 3D sounds
settings.summary: Whether the game plays positioned sound effects.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. Turning it off would silence most in-game effects.

settings.name: snd_enableReverb
settings.title: Reverb
settings.summary: Whether the game adds reverb to positioned sounds.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. TweakGuide says turning it off can improve performance.

settings.name: snd_enableStream
settings.title: Streamed sounds
settings.summary: Whether the game plays streamed sounds.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting.

settings.name: snd_errorOnMissing
settings.title: Error on missing sounds
settings.summary: Raises an error when a sound asset is missing.
settings.details: Off by default. A developer aid.

settings.name: snd_khz
settings.title: Sound quality
settings.summary: How detailed the game's sound is, from Low to High.
settings.details: The game opens its sound at 11, 22 or 44 kHz; any other number makes it use 22 kHz and print a warning. Higher gives finer sound at little performance cost. A change applies after the game restarts.

settings.name: snd_slaveFadeTime
settings.title: Volume fade time
settings.summary: How many milliseconds sounds take to fade when volumes are linked.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. The default is 500 milliseconds.

settings.name: snd_stereo
settings.title: Stereo sound
settings.summary: Plays sound in stereo instead of mono.
settings.details: On by default and latched, so a change applies after the game restarts. Mono removes direction from sound, which is a disadvantage when listening for footsteps.

settings.name: snd_touchStreamFilesOnLoad
settings.title: Preload streamed sounds
settings.summary: Reads streamed sound files in advance when a map loads.
settings.details: Off by default.

settings.name: snd_volume
settings.title: Game volume
settings.summary: How loud the game is, from silent to full.
settings.details: The value runs from 0 (silent) to 1 (full volume). The game's own Master Volume slider uses the same scale. This is separate from your Mac's output volume.

settings.name: stopspeed
settings.title: Stop speed
settings.summary: The speed threshold ground friction uses when slowing you down.
settings.details: The game protects this setting and the server's value is shared with every player, so it is not a player setting. The default is 100.

settings.name: sv_allowAnonymous
settings.title: Allow anonymous players
settings.summary: Lets players who hide their identity join a server you host.
settings.details: Off by default.

settings.name: sv_allowDownload
settings.title: Allow file downloads
settings.summary: Lets players download maps and mods straight from a server you host.
settings.details: On by default. Downloads through a web address are controlled separately.

settings.name: sv_allowedClan1
settings.title: Allowed clan 1
settings.summary: A text setting the game registers for a server you host.
settings.details: Its purpose is not documented.

settings.name: sv_allowedClan2
settings.title: Allowed clan 2
settings.summary: A text setting the game registers for a server you host.
settings.details: Its purpose is not documented.

settings.name: sv_cheats
settings.title: Cheat mode
settings.summary: Whether cheats are on for the current game.
settings.details: Protected: the game sets it itself and it can't be changed from here. While it is off, settings marked cheat-protected refuse changes. Match servers keep it off.

settings.name: sv_debugRate
settings.title: Show send timing
settings.summary: Prints how long each message would take to reach a player at their connection speed.
settings.details: A developer aid for servers you host.

settings.name: sv_debugReliableCmds
settings.title: Debug reliable commands
settings.summary: A developer switch the game registers for servers you host.
settings.details: No effect is documented for it.

settings.name: sv_disableClientConsole
settings.title: Disable player consoles
settings.summary: Stops players from using the console on a server you host.
settings.details: Off by default. The game sends this setting to players as part of the server's system information.

settings.name: sv_floodProtect
settings.title: Limit player commands
settings.summary: Limits each player's commands to one every 800 milliseconds on a server you host.
settings.details: On by default. Team changes and score requests are exempt, and extra commands are ignored without removing the player.

settings.name: sv_fps
settings.title: Server update rate
settings.summary: How many times per second a server you host runs the game.
settings.details: From 10 to 1,000, and 20 by default. It also caps how many updates per second any player can receive. zPAM's competitive rules default to 30 and support 40 on CoD2x. It is a server setting, not something you tune for yourself.

settings.name: sv_hostname
settings.title: Hosted server name
settings.summary: The name your server shows in the server list.
settings.details: It is shown in server lists and can be up to 32 characters in the game's Create Server menu. It is separate from your player name.

settings.name: sv_iwdNames
settings.title: Server game files
settings.summary: The names of the game files a server says it uses.
settings.details: The server sets this and your game treats it as read-only. While you are connected, the CoD2x client loads only these files plus the game's own.

settings.name: sv_iwds
settings.title: Server game file checks
settings.summary: Check codes for the game files a server says it uses.
settings.details: The server sets this and your game treats it as read-only.

settings.name: sv_keywords
settings.title: Server list keywords
settings.summary: Words that help players find a server you host in the server list.
settings.details: Empty by default.

settings.name: sv_kickBanTime
settings.title: Kick ban length
settings.summary: How many seconds a player stays banned after you kick them.
settings.details: From 0 to 3,600 seconds, 300 by default.

settings.name: sv_mapname
settings.title: Current map
settings.summary: The name of the map the server is running.
settings.details: The game fills this in itself and treats it as read-only.

settings.name: sv_mapRotation
settings.title: Map rotation
settings.summary: The list of maps and game types a server you host cycles through.
settings.details: Written as pairs of the words gametype and map followed by names, for example a game type, then a map. The server keeps the maps still to come in a separate setting.

settings.name: sv_mapRotationCurrent
settings.title: Maps still to come
settings.summary: The part of the map rotation a server you host has not played yet.
settings.details: The server fills this in itself.

settings.name: sv_maxclients
settings.title: Player slots
settings.summary: The most players your hosted server lets in.
settings.details: From 1 to 64, with 20 as the default. It is latched and applies after the map restarts. It only affects a server you host.

settings.name: sv_maxPing
settings.title: Highest allowed join ping
settings.summary: Turns away players whose ping is above this when they join (0 is off).
settings.details: It is checked only at the moment someone connects, not afterwards, and local network players are exempt. It affects a server you host, not your own connection.

settings.name: sv_maxRate
settings.title: Server bandwidth limit
settings.summary: The most data per second your server will send to any one player.
settings.details: 0 means no limit and the highest allowed is 25,000. The server uses the smaller of this and each player's own connection speed. zPAM sets it to 25,000.

settings.name: sv_minPing
settings.title: Lowest allowed join ping
settings.summary: Turns away players whose ping is below this when they join (0 is off).
settings.details: It is checked only at the moment someone connects, not afterwards, and local network players are exempt. It affects a server you host.

settings.name: sv_packet_info
settings.title: Packet info printing
settings.summary: A developer switch the game registers for servers you host.
settings.details: No effect is documented for it.

settings.name: sv_padPackets
settings.title: Pad update size
settings.summary: Adds extra bytes to every update a server you host sends, to test connection limits.
settings.details: A test aid with 0 as the default. Never use it on a live server.

settings.name: sv_paused
settings.title: Server paused
settings.summary: Whether the server is paused.
settings.details: The game keeps this up to date itself and treats it as read-only.

settings.name: sv_playerBroadcastLimit
settings.title: Send every player
settings.summary: While a server has this many players or fewer, it sends every player to every player, even out of sight.
settings.details: From 0 to 64, 15 by default, and 0 turns it off. It fixes missing sounds from players outside your view. CoD2x servers only.

settings.name: sv_privateClients
settings.title: Private slots
settings.summary: How many of a server's player slots need the private password.
settings.details: From 0 to 64, 0 by default. These slots come out of the server's total player slots, and the private password is set separately.

settings.name: sv_privatePassword
settings.title: Private slot password
settings.summary: The password for a server's private player slots.
settings.details: Treat it as private. Empty by default.

settings.name: sv_punkbuster
settings.title: PunkBuster (your server)
settings.summary: Whether the PunkBuster anti-cheat is switched on for a server you host.
settings.details: The game's Create Server menu shows it as PunkBuster, and the game protects it from changes here. This version of the game cannot show that a working PunkBuster service exists.

settings.name: sv_pure
settings.title: Require approved server files
settings.summary: Makes players on a server you host use only the same game files as the server.
settings.details: Players with modified game files are dropped. zPAM forces it on, and league rules forbid modified game files. It does not change checks on a server someone else hosts.

settings.name: sv_rateLimiter
settings.title: Limit server queries
settings.summary: Slows down floods of server-list and login-style requests to a server you host.
settings.details: CoD2x only. It limits each address and the total for status, info, challenge, remote console and disconnect requests.

settings.name: sv_rateLimiterRequestCount
settings.title: Limited requests
settings.summary: About how many requests the query limiter turned back in the last second.
settings.details: The game measures this once a second and treats it as read-only. It is not a setting.

settings.name: sv_rateLimiterUniqueIPCount
settings.title: Querying addresses
settings.summary: How many different addresses sent the server requests in the last second.
settings.details: The game measures this once a second and treats it as read-only. It is not a setting.

settings.name: sv_reconnectlimit
settings.title: Reconnect wait
settings.summary: How many seconds a player must wait before reconnecting to a server you host.
settings.details: From 0 to 1,800 seconds, 3 by default.

settings.name: sv_referencedIwdNames
settings.title: Referenced game file names
settings.summary: The names of the extra game files a server says clients need.
settings.details: The server sets this and your game treats it as read-only.

settings.name: sv_referencedIwds
settings.title: Referenced game file checks
settings.summary: Check codes for the extra game files a server says clients need.
settings.details: The server sets this and your game treats it as read-only.

settings.name: sv_running
settings.title: Server running
settings.summary: Whether a server is running on this computer.
settings.details: The game keeps this up to date itself and treats it as read-only.

settings.name: sv_serverid
settings.title: Server session number
settings.summary: A number that identifies the server's current session.
settings.details: The server sets this and your game treats it as read-only.

settings.name: sv_showAverageBPS
settings.title: Show average data rate
settings.summary: A developer switch the game registers for servers you host.
settings.details: No effect is documented for it.

settings.name: sv_showCommands
settings.title: Show player commands
settings.summary: A developer switch the game registers for servers you host.
settings.details: No effect is documented for it.

settings.name: sv_timeout
settings.title: Silent player timeout
settings.summary: How many seconds without data before a server you host drops a player.
settings.details: From 0 to 1,800 seconds, 240 by default. A vanished player can hold their slot for about this long.

settings.name: sv_voice
settings.title: Server voice chat
settings.summary: Turns voice chat on for a server you host.
settings.details: The game's Create Server menu has a Voice Chat switch for this. A player only gets voice if their connection speed is 5,000 or more.

settings.name: sv_voiceQuality
settings.title: Voice chat quality
settings.summary: How much detail a server's voice chat keeps.
settings.details: From 0 to 9, 1 by default. The server sends this to players as part of its system information.

settings.name: sv_wwwBaseURL
settings.title: Web download address
settings.summary: The web address players download files from on a server you host.
settings.details: Empty by default. zPAM asks for a valid address and suggests one for people who have none.

settings.name: sv_wwwDlDisconnected
settings.title: Download after disconnecting
settings.summary: Lets players keep downloading from the web address after they leave your server.
settings.details: Off by default. zPAM's server config turns it off.

settings.name: sv_wwwDownload
settings.title: Allow web downloads
settings.summary: Lets players download files from a web address for a server you host.
settings.details: Off by default. Players also need their own redirected downloads setting on. zPAM expects it on, with a valid web address, so its maps download quickly.

settings.name: sv_zombietime
settings.title: Dropped player hold time
settings.summary: How many seconds a dropped player's slot is held before it is freed.
settings.details: From 0 to 1,800 seconds, 2 by default. Leave it alone.

settings.name: sys_configSum
settings.title: System check sum
settings.summary: A checksum the game uses to decide when to run its hardware check again.
settings.details: The game protects it from changes here. Leave it alone.

settings.name: sys_cpuGHz
settings.title: Detected CPU speed
settings.summary: The processor speed the game detected, in GHz.
settings.details: The game protects it from changes here. It is hardware information.

settings.name: sys_gpu
settings.title: Detected graphics card
settings.summary: The graphics card the game detected.
settings.details: The game protects it from changes here. It is hardware information.

settings.name: sys_SSE
settings.title: SSE support
settings.summary: Whether the game treats your processor as supporting SSE.
settings.details: Not saved. TweakGuide says it should be on for all systems, and its value is not documented beyond that.

settings.name: sys_sysMB
settings.title: Detected memory
settings.summary: The system memory the game detected, in megabytes.
settings.details: The game protects it from changes here. TweakGuide notes it is often detected wrongly.

settings.name: timescale
settings.title: Game speed
settings.summary: How fast game time runs.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. The default is 1, and servers share it. It is used for demos and slow motion.

settings.name: ui_bigFont
settings.title: Big font scale
settings.summary: Scales one of the game's menu fonts.
settings.details: From 0 to 1. The defaults are 0.4, 0.55 and 0.25 for big, extra big and small fonts. It is purely cosmetic.

settings.name: ui_browserFriendlyfire
settings.title: Friendly-fire filter
settings.summary: The server browser's friendly-fire filter.
settings.details: The game's Filter menu offers All (-1), Off (0), On (1), Reflect (2) and Shared (3). This is only a browser filter.

settings.name: ui_browserKillcam
settings.title: Killcam filter
settings.summary: The server browser's killcam filter.
settings.details: The game's Filter menu offers All (-1), Off (0) and On (1). This is only a browser filter.

settings.name: ui_browserMod
settings.title: Mods filter
settings.summary: The server browser's filter for servers running mods.
settings.details: The game's Filter menu offers All (-1), No (0) and Yes (1). This is only a browser filter.

settings.name: ui_browserShowDedicated
settings.title: Dedicated servers only
settings.summary: Lists only dedicated servers in the server browser.
settings.details: This is the game's own server browser filter, set from its Filter menu, and it is separate from the launcher's browser filters.

settings.name: ui_browserShowEmpty
settings.title: Show empty servers
settings.summary: Includes servers with no players in the server browser.
settings.details: This is the game's own server browser filter, set from its Filter menu, and it is separate from the launcher's browser filters.

settings.name: ui_browserShowFull
settings.title: Show full servers
settings.summary: Includes servers with no free slots in the server browser.
settings.details: This is the game's own server browser filter, set from its Filter menu, and it is separate from the launcher's browser filters.

settings.name: ui_browserShowNoPassword
settings.title: Servers without passwords
settings.summary: Includes servers that need no password in the server browser.
settings.details: This is the game's own server browser filter, set from its Filter menu, and it is separate from the launcher's browser filters.

settings.name: ui_browserShowPassword
settings.title: Servers with passwords
settings.summary: Includes password-protected servers in the server browser.
settings.details: This is the game's own server browser filter, set from its Filter menu, and it is separate from the launcher's browser filters.

settings.name: ui_browserShowPunkBuster
settings.title: PunkBuster filter
settings.summary: The server browser's filter for PunkBuster servers.
settings.details: The game's Filter menu offers All (-1), Off (0) and On (1). This is only a browser filter.

settings.name: ui_browserShowPure
settings.title: Pure servers only
settings.summary: Lists only servers that require matching game files in the server browser.
settings.details: This is the game's own server browser filter, set from its Filter menu, and it is separate from the launcher's browser filters.

settings.name: ui_currentMap
settings.title: Selected map
settings.summary: A number the game's menus remember.
settings.details: The menus save this themselves. It is not a setting to tune.

settings.name: ui_currentNetMap
settings.title: Selected network map
settings.summary: A number the game's menus remember.
settings.details: The menus save this themselves. It is not a setting to tune.

settings.name: ui_dedicated
settings.title: Hosted server mode
settings.summary: Chooses how the in-game Create Server menu starts a server.
settings.details: The game's menu offers No (0), LAN (1) and Internet (2). The separate dedicated-server program is a different way to start a server.

settings.name: ui_extraBigFont
settings.title: Extra big font scale
settings.summary: Scales one of the game's menu fonts.
settings.details: From 0 to 1. The defaults are 0.4, 0.55 and 0.25 for big, extra big and small fonts. It is purely cosmetic.

settings.name: ui_gametype
settings.title: Selected game type
settings.summary: A number the game's menus remember.
settings.details: The menus save this themselves. It is not a setting to tune.

settings.name: ui_joinGametype
settings.title: Join game type filter
settings.summary: A number the game's menus remember.
settings.details: The menus save this themselves. It is not a setting to tune.

settings.name: ui_multiplayer
settings.title: Multiplayer menus
settings.summary: Whether the game's menus are in multiplayer mode.
settings.details: The game treats this as read-only and sets it itself.

settings.name: ui_netGametype
settings.title: Hosted game type number
settings.summary: A number the game's menus remember.
settings.details: The menus save this themselves. It is not a setting to tune.

settings.name: ui_netGametypeName
settings.title: Hosted game type name
settings.summary: The game type name the in-game Create Server menu remembers.
settings.details: The menu fills this in itself, and game scripts decide which game types exist.

settings.name: ui_netSource
settings.title: Server list source
settings.summary: A number the game's menus remember.
settings.details: The menus save this themselves. It is not a setting to tune.

settings.name: ui_playerProfileAlreadyChosen
settings.title: Profile already chosen
settings.summary: Records that a player profile has been chosen.
settings.details: The game sets this itself.

settings.name: ui_playerProfileCount
settings.title: Profile count
settings.summary: How many player profiles the game found.
settings.details: The game treats this as read-only and sets it itself.

settings.name: ui_playerProfileNameNew
settings.title: New profile name
settings.summary: The name typed into the game's profile-creation box.
settings.details: The game's own box takes up to 14 characters. Config Studio checks profile names separately.

settings.name: ui_playerProfileSelected
settings.title: Selected profile
settings.summary: The profile selected in the profile menu.
settings.details: The game treats this as read-only and sets it itself.

settings.name: ui_serverStatusTimeOut
settings.title: Server status timeout
settings.summary: How many milliseconds the server list waits for a server's status.
settings.details: The default is 7,000 milliseconds.

settings.name: ui_smallFont
settings.title: Small font scale
settings.summary: Scales one of the game's menu fonts.
settings.details: From 0 to 1. The defaults are 0.4, 0.55 and 0.25 for big, extra big and small fonts. It is purely cosmetic.

settings.name: version
settings.title: Build information
settings.summary: The game's build description.
settings.details: The game treats this as read-only and sets it itself. The registered default is empty and the game fills it in at start-up. The CoD2x build changes the build name and date.

settings.name: vid_xpos
settings.title: Window left position
settings.summary: Where the game window sits from the left of the screen when windowed.
settings.details: The game saves it every time you move the window. The range is -4,096 to 4,096.

settings.name: vid_ypos
settings.title: Window top position
settings.summary: Where the game window sits from the top of the screen when windowed.
settings.details: The game saves it every time you move the window. The range is -4,096 to 4,096.

settings.name: viewlog
settings.title: Console log overlay
settings.summary: Shows the developer console log over the picture.
settings.details: The game protects this setting: it only changes with cheats on, so it is not a player setting. It runs from 0 to 2.

settings.name: voice_deadChat
settings.title: Hear dead players
settings.summary: Lets you hear the voice chat of dead players.
settings.details: Off by default.

settings.name: voice_global
settings.title: Global voice chat
settings.summary: Makes voice chat audible to everyone.
settings.details: Off by default.

settings.name: voice_localEcho
settings.title: Hear yourself
settings.summary: Plays your own voice back to you.
settings.details: Off by default.

settings.name: winvoice_mic_mute
settings.title: Mute microphone
settings.summary: Mutes your microphone in voice chat.
settings.details: On by default. It is separate from your Mac's microphone mute.

settings.name: winvoice_mic_reclevel
settings.title: Microphone level
settings.summary: How loudly your microphone is recorded for voice chat.
settings.details: It runs from 0 to 65,535 and the default is the maximum. The game's Record Level slider uses the same range. It is separate from your Mac's microphone setting.

settings.name: winvoice_mic_scaler
settings.title: Microphone scale
settings.summary: A scale applied to your microphone signal in voice chat.
settings.details: From 0.25 to 2, and 1 by default.

settings.name: winvoice_save_voice
settings.title: Save received voice
settings.summary: Saves voice chat you receive to disk.
settings.details: Off by default. A debugging aid.
